title: Forecast with explicit uncertainty
description: Check history, seasonality, missing periods and structural changes.
accomplishes: Check history, seasonality, missing periods and structural changes. Compare a simple baseline with justified alternatives. Define backtesting and uncertainty communication. Do not invent forecast accuracy or present a point estimate as a certain future outcome.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Forecast with explicit uncertainty.

Input context:
- TIME SERIES: [TIME SERIES]
- HORIZON: [HORIZON]
- KNOWN CHANGES: [KNOWN CHANGES]
- PURPOSE: [PURPOSE]

Check history, seasonality, missing periods and structural changes. Compare a simple baseline with justified alternatives. Define backtesting and uncertainty communication. Do not invent forecast accuracy or present a point estimate as a certain future outcome.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Appointment forecast plan
First compare a recent-average baseline with a seasonal baseline if enough history exists. Hold out a suitable period and explain how missing bookings are handled. Capacity and planned closures may limit useful demand forecasts. Without actual evaluation, the output remains a plan; no prediction interval, accuracy score or guaranteed volume is reported.
